question: In the story 'Poets and Pancakes', what exactly does the word 'Pancake' refer to? 🥞
options: A popular breakfast item served in the studio canteen 🍽️
The brand name of the make-up material used in Gemini Studios 💄
A famous movie produced by the studio 🎬
The nickname of the studio boss 🧔
answer: The brand name of the make-up material used in Gemini Studios 💄
explanation: Spot on! 'Pancake' was the brand name of the thick make-up material that Gemini Studios bought in truckloads to make the actors look presentable on camera! 🎥
hint: It has nothing to do with food in this context.

question: Who is the author of the memoir 'Poets and Pancakes'? ✍️
answer: Asokamitran 🖋️
explanation: Brilliant! Asokamitran, a famous Tamil writer, wrote this humorous memoir about his years working at Gemini Studios in Chennai. 🌟
hint: He worked at Gemini Studios for several years.

question: Where was the make-up department of Gemini Studios located? 🏢
options: In the basement of the boss's house 🏠
In a building believed to have been Robert Clive's stables 🐎
In a newly constructed glass tower 🏙️
answer: In a building believed to have been Robert Clive's stables 🐎
explanation: Awesome! The make-up department was located upstairs in a building that was rumoured to have once been the stables of Robert Clive. 🐴
hint: It has a historical connection to a famous British officer's horses.

question: What did the make-up room look like with all its incandescent lights and mirrors? 💡
answer: A hair-cutting salon ✂️
explanation: Perfect! The author humorously compares the make-up room to a hair-cutting salon because of the many mirrors and bright incandescent lights that subjected the actors to 'fiery misery'. 🔥
hint: Think of a place where you sit in front of mirrors to get groomed.

question: What does Asokamitran mean when he says the make-up department was an example of 'national integration'? 🇮🇳
options: The department was headed by people from various different states over time 🗺️
answer: The department was headed by people from various different states over time 🗺️
explanation: Exactly! Long before A.I.R. or Doordarshan broadcast national integration, the make-up department achieved it by having a Bengali, a Maharashtrian, a Kannadiga, an Andhra, a Christian, and an Anglo-Burmese working together! 🤝
hint: It involves people from many different parts of India working together.

question: Who did the chief make-up man attend to in the strict hierarchy of the department? 👑
answer: The chief actors and actresses ⭐
explanation: Spot on! There was a strict hierarchy. The chief make-up man only worked on the faces of the main heroes and heroines of the film. 🎬
hint: He handled the most important people on the set.

question: Whose face did the 'office boy' in the make-up department paint? 🎨
answer: The crowd players 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
explanation: Great job! The office boy was in charge of slapping make-up onto the faces of the crowd players (extras) using a giant mixing vessel. 🥣
hint: He handled the large groups of extras in the background.

question: Was the 'office boy' actually a young boy? 👦
options: No, he was a forty-year-old man 👨
Yes, he was an eight-year-old child 🧒
No, he was an eighty-year-old man 👴
answer: No, he was a forty-year-old man 👨
explanation: Awesome! The term is deeply ironic. He was not a boy at all, but a frustrated forty-year-old man who hadn't achieved his dreams. 🕰️
hint: He had been working there for many years and was middle-aged.

question: What did the office boy originally hope to become when he joined Gemini Studios? 🌟
options: A star actor, top screen writer, or director 🎬
answer: A star actor, top screen writer, or director 🎬
explanation: Fantastic! He joined with big dreams of becoming a star actor, a top screen writer, director, or lyricist, but ended up merely painting the crowd players. 😔
hint: He wanted to be famous and creatively involved in the films.

question: What was the author's specific job at Gemini Studios? 📰
options: Tearing up newspapers and filing clippings ✂️
answer: Tearing up newspapers and filing clippings ✂️
explanation: Correct! Asokamitran's job was to sit in a cubicle, cut out newspaper clippings on a wide variety of subjects, and store them in files. 📂
hint: He worked with scissors, newspapers, and files.

question: Why did people at the studio think the author was doing 'next to nothing'? 🤷
options: He was always sleeping in his cubicle 😴
His job of cutting newspapers looked like useless work to others ✂️
He never showed up to work on time ⏰
He just watched movies all day 🍿
answer: His job of cutting newspapers looked like useless work to others ✂️
explanation: Spot on! Because he just sat at a desk tearing up newspapers all day, everyone, including the boss, thought his job was trivial and that he was basically doing nothing. 📰
hint: His task did not look like physically demanding or creative work.

question: Who did the office boy blame for all his woes, ignominy, and neglect? 😠
answer: Kothamangalam Subbu 🎬
explanation: Brilliant! The office boy directed all his anger and frustration at Kothamangalam Subbu, who was the No. 2 at Gemini Studios, feeling that Subbu had stolen his opportunities. 🔥
hint: He blamed the man who was officially No. 2 at the studio.

question: Why did the office boy feel he was better than Subbu? 🎓
options: He believed he had better formal education and poetry skills 📚
He was younger and better looking 👦
He belonged to a higher caste 👑
answer: He believed he had better formal education and poetry skills 📚
explanation: Awesome! The office boy felt superior because he was somewhat educated and wrote poetry, whereas Subbu had little formal education. 📖
hint: It relates to his schooling and literary aspirations.

question: What advantage did Kothamangalam Subbu have that helped his career, according to the narrator? 🕉️
options: He was born a Brahmin, granting him exposure to affluent situations 📿
He had an acting degree from London 🇬🇧
answer: He was born a Brahmin, granting him exposure to affluent situations 📿
explanation: Perfect! The author notes that Subbu being a Brahmin gave him an edge by providing him exposure to more affluent situations and people right from the start. 🌅
hint: It relates to the traditional social hierarchy.

question: Which of these best describes Subbu's personality? 😊
answer: Cheerful, loyal, and highly creative 🌟
explanation: Spot on! Subbu was constantly cheerful, endlessly creative in solving film problems, and incredibly loyal to the Boss, which made him indispensable. 💡
hint: He always had a solution for the producer and always looked happy.

question: What would Subbu do when a producer said, 'I don't know how to do this scene'? 🎬
options: Tell him to cancel the movie 🚫
Come up with at least fourteen different ways to shoot it 🧠
Walk away and take a break ☕
Ask the office boy for help 👦
answer: Come up with at least fourteen different ways to shoot it 🧠
explanation: Exactly! Subbu was a creative genius. If a producer was stuck, Subbu would instantly provide numerous creative alternatives to shoot a scene! 📽️
hint: He provided a large number of creative alternatives.

question: Despite being a successful poet and novelist, what was Subbu's primary focus? 🎥
answer: Films and serving the Boss 🎬
explanation: Fantastic! Even though he was a talented writer and poet, he devoted all his energy and creativity to filmmaking and his absolute loyalty to The Boss. 🤝
hint: He dedicated his life to the studio's main business.

question: What was the name of the acclaimed novel written by Subbu? 📖
answer: Thillana Mohanambal 💃
explanation: Brilliant! Subbu wrote the sprawling novel 'Thillana Mohanambal', which brilliantly captured the mood and characters of the early 20th century. 🎭
hint: It has a traditional South Indian title.

question: How did Subbu act when he played subordinate roles in films? 🎭
options: He performed better than the lead actors ⭐
answer: He performed better than the lead actors ⭐
explanation: Awesome! Subbu never aspired for lead roles, but whenever he played a supporting character, he often out-performed the main heroes! 🏆
hint: He was surprisingly good and often outshone the stars.

question: Why did the office boy hate Subbu so much? 😡
options: Subbu was closer to the Boss and seemed to have everything the office boy wanted 🌟
Subbu fired him from his previous job 🏢
Subbu made fun of his poetry 📝
answer: Subbu was closer to the Boss and seemed to have everything the office boy wanted 🌟
explanation: Spot on! The office boy was intensely jealous because Subbu was successful, beloved by the Boss, and had achieved the creative respect the office boy craved. 💔
hint: It was a matter of intense jealousy regarding success and proximity to the Boss.

question: In which department was the Legal Adviser officially placed? ⚖️
answer: The Story Department 📜
explanation: Correct! Ironically, the lawyer was a part of the Story Department, which consisted of poets and writers. 🖋️
hint: He was among the poets and writers.

question: How did the Legal Adviser stand out in his dress compared to the other members of the Story Department? 👔
options: He wore pants, a tie, and a coat, while everyone else wore khadi dhoti 👔
He wore shorts and a t-shirt 🩳
answer: He wore pants, a tie, and a coat, while everyone else wore khadi dhoti 👔
explanation: Great job! While all the poets wore uniform khadi dhotis (Gandhian style), the legal adviser looked completely out of place in his Western pants and tie. 👞
hint: He dressed in a Western style.

question: What did the Legal Adviser do that abruptly ended the career of a brilliant but temperamental actress? 🎤
options: He secretly switched on recording equipment while she was having a temper tantrum 📼
He cast someone else in her movie 🎬
answer: He secretly switched on recording equipment while she was having a temper tantrum 📼
explanation: Perfect! When she blew up on set, he quietly recorded her. When he played it back, she was so traumatized by her own voice that she never recovered. 🎙️
hint: He used a piece of audio technology against her.

question: Because of his actions, what was the Legal Adviser known as by the others? 🙃
options: The exact opposite of a legal adviser (an illegal adviser) 🚫
The smartest man in the studio 🧠
answer: The exact opposite of a legal adviser (an illegal adviser) 🚫
explanation: Exactly! Instead of getting people out of trouble, he unknowingly brought ruin to an innocent actress, earning him a reputation for being the opposite of a helper. 🤦
hint: It is an ironic title based on his actual job.

question: What happened to the lawyer when the Boss eventually closed down the Story Department? 🚪
options: He lost his job, which was rare for a lawyer to lose his job because poets were fired 📉
answer: He lost his job, which was rare for a lawyer to lose his job because poets were fired 📉
explanation: Awesome! The irony here is brilliant—a lawyer lost his job simply because a group of poets was asked to go home! 📜
hint: He suffered the same fate as the poets.

question: Most people in Gemini Studios wore Khadi and worshipped Gandhiji. What was their view on Communism? 🚫
options: They were strong supporters of it ✊
They didn't know what it was 🤷
They hated it, viewing a Communist as a godless man with no filial or conjugal love 👿
answer: They hated it, viewing a Communist as a godless man with no filial or conjugal love 👿
explanation: Spot on! The people at the studio were Gandhiites and viewed Communists as heartless, godless people who wouldn't hesitate to kill their own parents. 🛑
hint: They had a very strong, negative prejudice against it.

question: Which international group visited Gemini Studios in 1952? 🌍
answer: Frank Buchman's Moral Re-Armament army (MRA) 🎭
explanation: Brilliant! The MRA, essentially a counter-communist international theatrical group of about 200 people, was hosted warmly by Gemini Studios. 🎪
hint: They were an international anti-communist theater group.

question: Which two plays presented by the MRA became very famous in Madras? 🎭
options: Jotham Valley and The Forgotten Factor 🌄
Waiting for Godot and The Crucible 🕰️
answer: Jotham Valley and The Forgotten Factor 🌄
explanation: Perfect! 'Jotham Valley' and 'The Forgotten Factor' were staged perfectly and ran for multiple shows, leaving a lasting impact on Tamil theater. 🎟️
hint: One has 'Valley' in the name and the other has 'Factor'.

question: What specific theatrical technique did the Tamil plays copy from the MRA's 'Jotham Valley'? 🌅
options: A bare stage, a white background curtain, and a tune played on the flute 🎵
answer: A bare stage, a white background curtain, and a tune played on the flute 🎵
explanation: Awesome! For years after the MRA left, almost all Tamil plays adopted their minimalist sunset and sunrise staging style—a white curtain and a flute tune. 🌇
hint: It involved a minimalist set design for a sunset/sunrise scene.

question: What was the underlying political purpose of the MRA's world tour, according to the author? 🌍
options: To find new actors for Hollywood 🎬
answer: To spread anti-Communist ideology 🚫
explanation: Exactly! The author later realized that the MRA was a kind of international counter-movement to international Communism, which was gaining ground in South India at the time. 🛑
hint: They were heavily against a certain political ideology.

question: Sometime after the MRA left, Gemini Studios welcomed another special guest. Who was he? 🇬🇧
answer: An English poet (or editor) 📜
explanation: Spot on! A tall Englishman, who was either a poet or an editor, visited the studio, causing great confusion because no one knew exactly who he was! 🤷
hint: He was a literary figure from England.

question: Why was the English poet's speech at Gemini Studios a complete disaster? 🗣️
options: The audience could not understand a word he said due to his accent and subject matter 😕
answer: The audience could not understand a word he said due to his accent and subject matter 😕
explanation: Brilliant! He spoke about the thrills and travails of being an English poet to an audience of simple Tamil film workers, and his heavy accent made it impossible for them to understand him. 🤦
hint: It was a severe communication breakdown.

question: What did the author say was the 'bafflement' regarding the English poet's visit? 🤔
options: Why he was given so much food 🍲
What an English poet was doing in a film studio that made simple Tamil films 🎬
Why he didn't write a script for them 📝
Why he refused to wear make-up 💄
answer: What an English poet was doing in a film studio that made simple Tamil films 🎬
explanation: Great job! The sheer absurdity of an English poet addressing people whose lives centered around making simple Tamil films was a source of huge bafflement and irony. 🤪
hint: It relates to the complete mismatch between the guest and the audience.

question: Years later, after leaving Gemini Studios, the author saw a notice in 'The Hindu' about a short story contest organized by a British periodical. What was the periodical's name? 📰
answer: The Encounter 📖
explanation: Perfect! 'The Encounter' was a British periodical that was running a short story contest, which prompted the author to visit the British Council Library. 🏛️
hint: It means a sudden or unexpected meeting.

question: When the author went to the British Council Library to find out about 'The Encounter', whose name did he see as the editor? 😲
answer: Stephen Spender 🖋️
explanation: Awesome! The moment he read the editor's name—Stephen Spender—he finally solved the mystery of the tall Englishman who had visited Gemini Studios years ago! 🎉
hint: His initials are S.S.

question: How did Asokamitran feel when he discovered Stephen Spender was the editor? 💡
options: He felt a sudden, thrilling connection, as if he had found a long-lost brother 🤝
He felt sad for the poet 😢
answer: He felt a sudden, thrilling connection, as if he had found a long-lost brother 🤝
explanation: Spot on! Discovering Spender's identity brought back a rush of memories, and he felt a warm, personal connection, as if a great mystery had been solved. ✨
hint: He felt very happy and connected.

question: What book did the author buy years later for fifty paise at a pavement shop in Mount Road? 📚
answer: The God That Failed 📖
explanation: Excellent! He bought 'The God That Failed', an essay collection by six famous writers describing their journey into Communism and their disillusioned return. 🛤️
hint: The title suggests a belief system that disappointed its followers.

question: Whose name did Asokamitran unexpectedly find among the authors of 'The God That Failed'? 🖋️
answer: Stephen Spender 📜
explanation: Brilliant! Seeing Stephen Spender's name in this anti-communist book finally explained the true purpose behind his mysterious visit to the anti-communist Gemini Studios! 💡
hint: It was the same English poet who visited the studio.

question: What literary device is heavily used by Asokamitran throughout the chapter to mock the studio's functioning? 🎭
answer: Humour and Satire 🃏
explanation: Spot on! The entire essay is a brilliant piece of humour and subtle satire, poking gentle fun at the egos, hypocrisies, and absurdities of the film industry. 🤣
hint: He uses comedy to point out the silly aspects of the studio.

question: According to the author, what is prose writing NOT meant for? ✍️
answer: A genius 🧠
explanation: Awesome! Asokamitran humorously states that prose writing is not and cannot be the true pursuit of a genius; it is meant for the patient, persevering drudge with a heart so shrunken it can't be broken! 😅
hint: He says it is meant for a 'drudge' instead of this.

question: Why did the narrator buy 'The God That Failed' at a reduced price? 💸
options: It was a student edition meant for the 50th anniversary of the Russian Revolution 🇷🇺
answer: It was a student edition meant for the 50th anniversary of the Russian Revolution 🇷🇺
explanation: Correct! It was a special, low-priced student edition printed in connection with the 50th Anniversary of the Russian Revolution, which is why it cost only 50 paise! 🪙
hint: It was a special edition for an anniversary.

question: Which word best describes the hierarchy in the make-up department? 🔼
answer: Strict and rigid 🧱
explanation: Perfect! The hierarchy was incredibly strict—the chief did the stars, the senior assistant did the secondary leads, the junior did the comedian, and the office boy did the crowd. No crossing lines! 📏
hint: It was very firmly established and not flexible.

question: What does the author's description of Subbu tell us about human nature in workplaces? 🏢
options: Hard work always gets rewarded equally 🏆
Creativity and loyalty often breed jealousy among less successful peers 🐍
answer: Creativity and loyalty often breed jealousy among less successful peers 🐍
explanation: Brilliant! The dynamic between the cheerful, successful Subbu and the bitter, jealous office boy perfectly captures how workplace success can breed intense envy. 💔
hint: Look at the relationship between Subbu and the office boy.

question: The people at Gemini Studios believed that a Communist would...? 👿
options: Have no hesitation in killing his own parents or children 🔪
answer: Have no hesitation in killing his own parents or children 🔪
explanation: Spot on! Influenced by the political climate and MRA propaganda, they naively believed a Communist was a monster devoid of all familial love. 🛑
hint: They thought a Communist was completely ruthless and lacked family love.

question: What irony is present in the Legal Adviser's story? ⚖️
options: His job title implied he offered legal protection, but his actions ruined a career 🚫
He was a poet in disguise 🎭
answer: His job title implied he offered legal protection, but his actions ruined a career 🚫
explanation: Awesome! Situational irony occurs here because the person hired to protect people legally ended up causing the permanent downfall of an innocent actress. 🎭
hint: His actions contradicted his job title.

question: How did Asokamitran manage his rejections when submitting his prose writing? 📮
options: He prepared his manuscript, sent it off, and patiently accepted rejection as a 'drudge' 🐢
answer: He prepared his manuscript, sent it off, and patiently accepted rejection as a 'drudge' 🐢
explanation: Great job! He explains that a prose writer must have a thick skin, patiently enduring rejection and continuing to send manuscripts without heartbreak. 📝
hint: He showed immense patience and perseverance.

question: What does the chapter title 'Poets and Pancakes' signify? 🥞
options: The diet of the studio workers 🍽️
The contrast between the literary aspirations of the writers and the superficial, cosmetic reality of film-making 🎭
A famous poem written by Subbu 📜
The two departments that fought the most 🥊
answer: The contrast between the literary aspirations of the writers and the superficial, cosmetic reality of film-making 🎭
explanation: Perfect! 'Poets' represents the high-minded literary folks in the Story Dept, while 'Pancakes' represents the thick make-up and superficial illusions of the film industry. A brilliant contrast! ✨
hint: It highlights the difference between high art and cosmetic illusion.

question: Who was the founder and boss of Gemini Studios? 🧔
answer: S.S. Vasan 🏢
explanation: Spot on! Mr. S.S. Vasan was the influential founder and boss of Gemini Studios, a man to whom Subbu was entirely dedicated. 🌟
hint: His name starts with S.S.

question: What made the Gemini Studios' poets 'khadi-clad' Gandhiites? 🧶
options: They were forced by the police 👮
It was the fashion trend in London 🇬🇧
They wore homespun cloth and admired Gandhi, showing their political leanings 🇮🇳
answer: They wore homespun cloth and admired Gandhi, showing their political leanings 🇮🇳
explanation: Awesome! Wearing khadi was a political and social statement of supporting Mahatma Gandhi and the nationalist movement. 🕊️
hint: It reflected their admiration for a prominent Indian freedom fighter.

question: Ultimately, the essay 'Poets and Pancakes' is an excerpt from which larger book by Asokamitran? 📖
answer: My Years with Boss 🏢
explanation: Brilliant! This wonderful chapter is a delightful excerpt from Asokamitran's larger book 'My Years with Boss', documenting his time under S.S. Vasan. 🎉
hint: The title refers to his time working for his employer.
